#!/bin/bash
# PreToolUse(Read) hook (personal): auto-downscale oversized images to a token
# budget and rewrite the Read to point at the downscaled copy.
#
# WHY THIS GATES ON PIXELS, NOT BYTES
# -----------------------------------
# The previous revision fired on `stat` file size > 150 KB and only emitted a
# reminder. Both halves were wrong, and the transcripts prove it:
#
#   * Anthropic bills an image at (w*h)/750 tokens after fitting the long edge
#     to 1568 px. File size does not appear in that formula at all. Measured in
#     session e5d3e591: pop.png was 589,400 b64 bytes at 1000x646 = 861 tokens,
#     while activity-approval-tall.png was 120,960 b64 bytes at 1360x1080 =
#     1533 tokens. The 4.9x SMALLER file cost 78% MORE tokens. A size gate
#     ranks images in almost the reverse of what they cost.
#   * Base64 image bytes run 240-525 bytes per billed token; text runs ~3.6.
#     So "% of transcript bytes" overstates image token share by 60-130x.
#     Images were 88-99% of tool-result BYTES in the two heaviest sessions but
#     only 13.9% and 3.8% of context TOKENS.
#   * Reminder-only did not work. Both sessions read full-resolution images
#     anyway, with this hook installed and firing.
#
# Rewriting is what actually saves anything, and 2.1.224 supports it:
# hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput is in the PreToolUse zod schema and the
# dispatcher assigns it over the original tool input.
#
# Modelled against the two sessions at IMAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET=600, this cuts
# amortized image cost by 31% and 36% (2.18M and 2.60M cache-read tokens),
# which is ~2-4% of each session's total billed context. Images are a real but
# secondary lever -- Bash command+output is 51% of amortized cost in both.
#
# NEVER blocks. Exits 0 on every path; any failure falls through to the
# original, unmodified Read.
set -u

input=$(cat)

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v sips >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

path=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty' 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
[ -n "$path" ] || exit 0

lower=$(printf '%s' "$path" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

# sips can only re-encode these. webp/gif/heic pass through untouched.
case "$lower" in
  *.png|*.jpg|*.jpeg) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

# EXEMPTIONS: the image is the deliverable or fine detail is the point.
# `full` is the documented escape hatch -- copy to <name>-full.png to opt out.
case "$lower" in
  *frame*|*render*|*-full.*|*_full.*|*.mp4*) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Never recurse on our own output.
case "$path" in
  */.claude/cache/downscaled/*) exit 0 ;;
esac

[ -f "$path" ] && [ -r "$path" ] || exit 0

budget="${IMAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET:-600}"
case "$budget" in ''|*[!0-9]*) budget=600 ;; esac
[ "$budget" -ge 50 ] || budget=600

dim=$(sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight "$path" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
w=$(printf '%s' "$dim" | awk '/pixelWidth/{print $2}')
h=$(printf '%s' "$dim" | awk '/pixelHeight/{print $2}')
case "${w:-x}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;; esac
case "${h:-x}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;; esac
[ "$w" -gt 0 ] && [ "$h" -gt 0 ] || exit 0

# Replicate Anthropic's billing geometry: fit long edge to 1568, then clamp
# total area to 1.15 Mpx, then tokens = area/750. Emit the current cost and the
# long edge that would land on the budget.
read -r cur_tok target < <(awk -v w="$w" -v h="$h" -v B="$budget" '
BEGIN {
  long = (w > h) ? w : h;
  s = (long > 1568) ? 1568.0 / long : 1.0;
  W = w * s; H = h * s;
  if (W * H > 1150000) { k = sqrt(1150000.0 / (W * H)); W *= k; H *= k; }
  t = (W * H) / 750.0;
  L = (W > H) ? W : H;
  if (t <= B) { print int(t), 0; exit }
  # tokens scale with area, so linear dimension scales with sqrt.
  nt = int(L * sqrt(B / t));
  if (nt < 64) nt = 64;
  print int(t), nt;
}')

case "${target:-0}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;; esac
[ "$target" -gt 0 ] || exit 0          # already within budget
[ "$target" -lt "$((w > h ? w : h))" ] || exit 0

# Content-addressed cache: same file (size+mtime) at the same target reuses the
# encode, so re-reading one screenshot 5 times costs one sips run.
size=$(stat -Lf%z "$path" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
mtime=$(stat -Lf%m "$path" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
key=$(printf '%s|%s|%s|%s' "$path" "$size" "$mtime" "$target" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-16)
[ -n "$key" ] || exit 0

cache="$HOME/.claude/cache/downscaled"
mkdir -p "$cache" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
base=$(basename "$path")
out="$cache/${base%.*}-${target}px-${key}.${base##*.}"

if [ ! -f "$out" ]; then
  sips -Z "$target" "$path" --out "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f "$out" 2>/dev/null; exit 0; }
fi
[ -s "$out" ] || { rm -f "$out" 2>/dev/null; exit 0; }

# Report the delivered cost from the ACTUAL output, not the prediction.
odim=$(sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight "$out" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
ow=$(printf '%s' "$odim" | awk '/pixelWidth/{print $2}')
oh=$(printf '%s' "$odim" | awk '/pixelHeight/{print $2}')
case "${ow:-x}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;; esac
case "${oh:-x}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;; esac
new_tok=$(awk -v w="$ow" -v h="$oh" 'BEGIN{printf "%d", (w*h)/750.0}')

MSG="Auto-downscaled: reading a ${ow}x${oh} copy of this ${w}x${h} image (~${new_tok} tokens instead of ~${cur_tok}; images bill at w*h/750, independent of file size). Layout, color and anything above ~11px of UI text survive this. If you specifically need fine detail (pixel diffing, small dense text, exact 1px borders), copy the original to a path containing '-full' and Read that to bypass this hook."

jq -n --arg p "$out" --arg m "$MSG" '{
  hookSpecificOutput: {
    hookEventName: "PreToolUse",
    updatedInput: {file_path: $p},
    additionalContext: $m
  }
}'
exit 0

## Your suspicion is refuted — but the fix is still worth shipping

**Bytes are not tokens.** Anthropic bills an image at `(w*h)/750` after fitting the long edge to 1568px. File size does not appear in that formula. Base64 image data runs 240–525 bytes per billed token; text runs ~3.6. That's a 60–130x distortion, and it's the whole reason the 88–95% figure looked alarming.

Decoding every PNG/JPEG header in both transcripts:

| | e5d3e591 | 259b2997 |
|---|---|---|
| image share of tool-result **bytes** | 99% | 97% |
| image share of context **tokens** | **13.9%** | **3.8%** |
| all images, total | 41,890 tok | 21,202 tok |

The concrete inversion, from your own transcript: `pop.png` was 589,400 b64 bytes at 1000x646 = **861 tok**; `activity-approval-tall.png` was 120,960 bytes at 1360x1080 = **1533 tok**. The 4.9x *smaller* file cost 78% *more*.

## Where the tokens actually are

Cache-read is quadratic — an item's real cost is size × turns it survives. Weighting every item by the API calls that followed it:

| category | e5d3e591 | 259b2997 |
|---|---|---|
| **Bash (cmd + output)** | **52.5%** | **50.8%** |
| Read output | 9.7% | 13.3% |
| **Images** | **13.3%** | **5.1%** |
| Edit/Write inputs | 11.4% | 13.2% |

Bash is the elephant in both, at ~51%. Floor (system+tools+CLAUDE.md+MEMORY.md) is ~53K tokens median across 110 sessions — 22% of the 237K average call.

## Candidate fixes, verdict

1. **PreToolUse rewrite — viable, shipped.** Confirmed in the 2.1.224 binary: `updatedInput` is in the PreToolUse zod schema (`updatedInput:Hn(N(),to()).optional()`) and the dispatcher assigns it. Shell hooks, not just the SDK handler.
2. **PostToolUse deletion — dead.** PostToolUse's schema exposes only `additionalContext`; it cannot rewrite or evict a result already in the transcript.
3. **Subagent isolation — works but wrong tool here.** Real for the 51% Bash lever, not needed for a 5–13% one.

## What I changed

`~/.claude/hooks/prefer-downscaled-image-read.sh` (−39/+111). Gate moved from `stat` size >150KB to **decoded pixel dimensions → estimated tokens**, and it now *rewrites* instead of nudging. Budget-600 default, content-addressed cache, `-full` escape hatch, exits 0 on every failure path.

The old gate was wrong in **both** directions on real files:

| file | old (size>150KB) | new (budget 600) |
|---|---|---|
| marquee.png — 98KB, **1045 tok** | **silent** ← missed the priciest image | rewrites → 599 tok |
| lenna.png — 474KB, **349 tok** | **fires** ← false positive | silent |
| screenshot.png — 211KB, 1008 tok | fires (nudge only) | rewrites → 598 tok |
| hero-**full**.png | fires | silent (exempt) |

**Live proof:** I asked to Read the 1400x560 marquee and received 1060x424 — argument rewritten, honored by Claude Code, and everything down to the ~10px "2d ago · Gmail" labels stayed legible. Also verified: sibling keys preserved (`offset`/`limit` survive the merge), cache reuse (cold 0.10s → warm 0.07s, identical output), recursion guard, and rc=0 on missing file / corrupt PNG / malformed JSON / empty stdin.

**Modeled saving:** 31% and 36% of amortized image cost (2.18M and 2.60M cache-read tokens on those two sessions) — **~2–4% of total billed context**, roughly 20–50M tokens/day at your 1,150.7M/24h. Real, but not the lever you were hoping for.

## Confidence

- **Measurement (95).** Decoded every image header directly; my amortization model reproduces the ranking, though it undercounts absolute cache-read ~2–3x because it omits the per-call floor and thinking tokens. Shares are sound; absolute totals are lower bounds.
- **`updatedInput` support (95).** Read the schema and dispatcher out of the binary, then confirmed live end-to-end.
- **Hook robustness (85).** 9 failure paths tested, plus live use. Not yet exercised across a full multi-hour session or on JPEG-heavy input.
- **The 51% Bash claim (80).** Consistent across both sessions, but n=2 and both are UI-development sessions.

## Suggested next actions

1. **Go after Bash — it's 10x the lever.** Same `updatedInput` mechanism can append `| head -c N` to `Bash.command`, but that changes exit codes and pipeline semantics. Safer first cut: cap only the read-only verbs (`git log/diff`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`) where truncation is harmless. Capping Bash output at 500 tok would have saved 17K/49K tokens flat, and far more amortized.
2. **Tune the budget.** I defaulted to 600. Budget-400 nearly doubles the saving (48–54% of image cost); worth one session at `IMAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET=400` to see if UI text stays readable.
3. **Re-run `amort.py` on a non-UI session** to test whether Bash-at-51% generalizes or is an artifact of these two.
4. **Consider the ~53K floor.** It's 22% of the average call and paid 6,026 times/day; MEMORY.md alone is 4.5K. Trimming it beats any tool-result optimization for short sessions.

content.text:
## #3 made sense — and it changed the answer

Ran it on three non-UI sessions. Bash generalizes, but two of my numbers were wrong:

| session | Bash (in+out) | Read.out | IMAGE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7b3373da (6290 calls) | 31.9% | **22.1%** | 2.0% |
| 76bd69b4 (4336) | 35.6% | **24.4%** | — |
| 9b2cbf0b (3682) | **56.9%** | 6.3% | — |
| e5d3e591 (UI) | 52.5% | 9.7% | 13.3% |
| 259b2997 (UI) | 50.8% | 13.3% | 5.1% |

`Read` output is far bigger than I credited, and **images collapse to ~2% outside UI sessions** — so the hook I shipped last turn is a UI-session-only lever, narrower than I presented it.

## #1: went after Bash, and the answer is not a hook

Rewriting `Bash.command` is the wrong mechanism, for three reasons I could only see after measuring:

- **The cost is volume, not size.** Median Bash output is 105–133 tokens across 1244–1765 calls. There's no fat tail to trim — results *under* 500 tokens carry 38–44% of the cost.
- **No verb to target.** `cd` prefixes are 38% of attributed cost (i.e. unattributable), and the genuinely expensive results are CI logs, vitest runs, and greps that are usually needed in full. Blind truncation causes re-runs that cost more than they save.
- **A supported cap already exists.** `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` defaults to **30,000 chars** (~8,300 tok/result; max 150k) and is in the settings-env allowlist. Claude Code's own truncation also tells the model it truncated, which a `| head` rewrite would not.

Bash-only, capped at 4000 chars (≈p95 of output size): **1.8–4.1%** saved, truncating just 2.3–3.3% of calls.

I also checked `CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (default 25,000) and am **not** recommending it: `Read` doesn't truncate, it *errors* — "Use offset and limit parameters" — so lowering it forces paging and likely nets to zero or worse.

## The lever that actually matters

Billed cache-read ≈ calls × average context, so the compaction ceiling dominates every per-result optimization. `autoCompactWindow` is a settings.json key (min 1e5, max 1e6). Simulated across all five sessions, then calibrated against each one's *measured* cache-read:

| autoCompactWindow | calibrated cache-read | reduction | compactions/session |
|---|---|---|---|
| current (~1M) | 4,609M | — | 0–2 |
| **400,000** | 2,352M | **49.0%** | 0–7 |
| 300,000 | 1,791M | 61.1% | 1–11 |
| 200,000 | 1,338M | 71.0% | 2–20 |

That's ~15x the image hook and ~12x the Bash cap. The tradeoff is real and it isn't free: 7b3373da would go from 2 compactions to 7, and every compaction loses detail. For your long autonomous PR-shipping sessions that's a quality risk, which is why I'd start at 400K rather than 200K.

## Blocked — needs you

The permission classifier denied my edit to `~/.claude/settings.json`, and I didn't route around it. The change to the existing `env` block, plus one new top-level key:

```json
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS": "60000",
    "BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH": "4000"
  },
  "autoCompactWindow": 400000,
```

Both take effect on restart. Or: `! claude config set autoCompactWindow 400000`

## Confidence

- **Bash-is-volume-not-size (90).** Percentiles and concentration curves computed directly on five sessions; consistent across UI and non-UI.
- **`BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` semantics (85).** Default and allowlist read out of the binary. I could not verify the 4000 value in practice — it needs a restart, so the truncation behavior at that setting is modeled, not observed.
- **autoCompactWindow gain (70).** The key and its bounds are confirmed in the zod schema, but the 49–71% range is a *simulation* — it assumes a 53K floor, a 15K summary re-seed, and flat 3.6 B/tok. Calibrating against measured cache-read corrects the worst of it, but this is the one number here I'd want a real A/B on before trusting.
- **Image hook (unchanged, 85).** Still verified end-to-end; just narrower in scope than I said.

## Next actions

1. **Apply the settings above, then A/B `autoCompactWindow`** — run one week at 400K and re-run `window.py` against the new transcripts to replace my simulated number with a measured one.
2. **Watch for compaction-induced rework.** If sessions start re-reading files they'd already read, 400K is too tight — that failure mode would show up as rising `Read.out` amortized cost, which the script already reports.
3. **Reconsider subagent isolation** (option 3 from your original brief) — I dismissed it too fast. It's the only fix that addresses the 38–44% of Bash cost sitting in small results, by keeping exploratory sweeps out of the parent window entirely.
4. Optionally set `IMAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET=400` for UI sessions specifically (48–54% of image cost vs 31–36% at the 600 default).

Scripts are in the scratchpad: `amort.py` (cost by category), `window.py` (compaction simulation), `conc.py` (concentration), `caps.py`, `verbs.py`.

content.text:
It's unrelated to tokens — different mechanism entirely. `CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS` is the auto-advance timeout for **AskUserQuestion**: if you don't answer within it, Claude Code submits on your behalf and continues (`tengu_ask_user_question_afk_auto_advance`).

Two details that matter for picking a value:

- On timeout it submits **whatever you'd partially selected** — the handler passes the current answer state with `hadPartialAnswers: Object.keys(w).length > 0`. It does not pick the recommended option for you. So a timeout on an untouched question advances on a non-answer.
- The countdown default is 20s (`ruv=20000`), clamped to `min(countdown, timeout)`. At your current 60s you get 40s of silence, then a 20s visible countdown.

So yes, I think 4 minutes is better for how you work. You reserve AskUserQuestion for decisions that are genuinely yours — your own AGENTS.md says to block only on irreversible actions or real user calls. Auto-advancing exactly those after 60 seconds defeats the reason for asking, and 60s is less time than it takes to read a four-option question with previews if you'd tabbed away at all.

The one case where 60s is right: if you set it deliberately so unattended sessions never stall. If that's why it's there, raising it to 240000 means an unattended session can now sit for 4 minutes per question instead of 1 — worth knowing before you change it, though sessions that ask several questions are the ones you probably want stalling anyway.

If you want the middle ground, raise the countdown alongside it so the warning window scales:

```json
"CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS": "240000",
"CLAUDE_AFK_COUNTDOWN_MS": "60000"
```

Confidence ~85 on the mechanism (read the handler and the env resolution out of the binary; I couldn't resolve the built-in default for the timeout itself, only the 20s countdown default). Zero measured impact on context or spend — it doesn't touch the levers from the earlier analysis.

`CLAUDE_AFK_TIMEOUT_MS` has nothing to do with session idling or token cost. It
is the deadline for **AskUserQuestion**: when it expires, Claude Code submits on
Burak's behalf and the run continues (`tengu_ask_user_question_afk_auto_advance`).

Two details that decide the right value:

- On expiry it submits **whatever was partially selected** — the handler passes

  question advances the run on a non-answer.

  clamped to `min(countdown, timeout)`.

Was 60000 (40s silent, then a 20s countdown). Raised 2026-08-07 to

decisions that are genuinely Burak's — auto-advancing exactly those after a
minute defeats the reason for asking, and 60s is less than the time to read a
four-option question with previews after tabbing away.

Tradeoff to remember if this ever needs reverting: a short timeout is the right
call ONLY if the goal is that unattended sessions never stall. At 240s an
unattended session can now sit 4 minutes per question — but sessions asking
several questions are usually the ones that should stall.
